title: Amberwood Academy — Classroom LLM pilot intake (scratchpad)
content:
Meeting capture (09/17)
Attendees: Riley (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood Solutions), Evan (Amberwood CTO), Priya (Amberwood Dir of PD), L. Thompson (Teacher pilot lead)
Quick TL;DR:
- Amberwood Academy wants a classroom assistant for grades 6–9: on-device hinting + hosted fallback, live teacher dashboard, and a student-facing chat widget embedded in LMS.
- Primary constraints: FERPA compliance (student PII cannot leave school VPC unless explicitly consented), intermittent connectivity (some classrooms have 3G fallback), strict token cost targets (pilot budget ~ $600/month), and real-time latency expectations (teacher dashboard updates <500ms for summaries).
- Pilot scope: 6 teachers, 120 students, 4-week trial. Start date targeted early Nov.

Raw call notes / fragments:
- Evan: "We need something that works when the Wi-Fi cuts — teachers can't lose conversation state mid-lesson."
- Priya: concerned about grading/plagiarism: "We want assistant to help scaffold responses but not to write full essays. Need detect/regulate outputs."
- Teacher: wants instant summarization of the last 10 student chats (dashboard) and a quick 'class pulse' score (confusion/confidence) per 15-minute block.

Functional requirements (initial):
1) Student chat widget embedded in LMS (LTI or iframe).
2) Local inference option: small quantized model on classroom edge box (NVIDIA Jetson Xavier-like or local server) for low-latency hinting and offline fallback.
3) Hosted Redwood API fallback when edge capacity unavailable.
4) Teacher dashboard: aggregated summaries, flagged risky outputs (safety/PII), per-student usage and token counts, ability to inject a correction or broadcast a prompt to whole class.
5) Audit logs (who asked what, redaction tokenization) retained per school policy for 6 months.
6) Prompt templates for scaffolded help (hint -> hint+example -> suggestion), with hooks for dynamic curriculum variables.
7) Access controls: per-class API keys, teacher override, student anonymous IDs (no PII in payloads).
8) Moderation and plagiarism detector integration (call with third-party vendor later).

Nonfunctional / performance targets:
- P95 response latency (edge): <120ms for single-turn hint (small context).
- P95 response latency (hosted fallback): <400ms for streaming short responses.
- Cost target: average token spend per student per month < 2k tokens (pilot billing must stay within $600).
- Uptime: teacher dashboard must be 99.9% during school hours.

Privacy & compliance notes (FERPA-focused):
- Amberwood legal: student identifiers cannot leave VPC unless encrypted under KMS and explicit parental consent logged.
- Proposed approach: strip identifiable fields at client before send; store mapping locally on Amberwood. If host fallback needed, send deidentified session id.
- Logging: store original prompts only in Amberwood's private deployment (or encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS) — Redwood Private suggested.
- Ask: does Amberwood have HSM/KMS? Evan: yes, via AWS KMS in their VPC (we need to validate key policies).

Edge/inference considerations (gotchas):
- Classroom boxes are mixed: 2x Jetson, 1x older Xeon microserver. We should provide a footprint matrix for model sizes (7B-quantized int8, 2GB cache) and expected batch behavior.
- Model warmup behavior: if teacher starts class after long idle, first requests spike latency — need prewarm strategy. Maybe schedule a 30s keepalive before class start time (teacher can hit "Start class" button).
- KV cache persistence: do we clear per-class period? Teachers want sessions isolated per lesson and cleared at EOD to avoid cross-day leakage.
- Tokenization differences between hosted and edge model variants: prompt length accounting mismatch could blow budget. Recommend unified tokenizer or careful token budgeting guidelines in README.

Safety / output control (teacher concerns):
- Must have guardrails to prevent hallucination of real student info or medical/legal advice.
- Allow configurable output templates: max response length, include "I might be wrong" prefix for uncertain answers.
- Flagging: students can flag an assistant response to teacher; flagged items show up in dashboard queue.

Proposed architecture (sketch):
- Client (LMS iframe) -> local inference box (if available) run quantized model via Redwood Private edge runtime -> if capacity/mode not available -> Redwood hosted API (via school VPC private endpoint) -> Teacher dashboard subscribes to event bus (Kafka/Redis) for aggregated summaries (no PII)
- Storage: student mappings and logs stored in Amberwood's S3 (encrypted, KMS). Redwood gets only deidentified telemetry for cost/health.

Prompt examples (for curriculum team):
- Hint 1 (scaffolded): "You are a study helper. Provide a one-sentence hint about why photosynthesis needs sunlight, without giving the full answer. If the student asks for more, offer an example experiment."
- Teacher broadcast template: "Class, start with warm-up: explain photosynthesis in 2 sentences. Students: submit your answer in the chat."
- Safety template: prepend to all assistant outputs: "This is an educational suggestion. Check with your teacher before using as final work."

Evaluation plan (pilot KPIs):
- Engagement: % students using assistant at least once/week (target 70% in week 1, 85% by week 4).
- Latency: P95 under targets above (measured by token/response).
- Cost: monthly spend per student <= $5 (pilot target).
- Quality: teacher-rated helpfulness (1–5) on random sample of 200 responses (target mean >= 4.0).
- Safety: number of flagged outputs per week (target <= 2/week during pilot).

Open questions / blockers (for follow-up):
- Q1: Confirm Amberwood's acceptable retention period for raw prompts when stored in Redwood Private. (Action: Maya to validate with Amberwood legal by 09/22)
- Q2: Edge hardware inventory + whether Amberwood can provide a Kubernetes node for private runtime or we ship a prebuilt Jetson container. (Action: Evan to send inventory CSV by 09/24)
- Q3: Does Amberwood want teacher-facing edit to logs? If yes, need RBAC for edits + audit trail. (Priya to confirm policy)
- Q4: Plagiarism detection vendor — do they want real text or embeddings? If embeddings, are they comfortable sending deidentified embeddings to vendor? (Riley to scope integration options)

Immediate next steps / action items (owners + dates):
- Send pilot scoping doc + estimated token budget and recommended model sizes to Amberwood (Riley) — due 09/19.
- Inventory request email template for edge machines (Maya) — due 09/20.
- Draft minimal privacy flow diagram showing where PII is stripped/encrypted (Priya) — due 09/22.
- Setup demo repo for teacher dashboard mock and embed widget (Evan + Riley) — initial demo by 09/29.
- Internal: run quick cost sim for 7B int8 vs hosted 13B perf/cost for 120 students (Evan + Solutions infra) — share numbers 09/26.

Notes to self (Riley):
- Build two short prompt sets: "scaffold hints" and "class summary" for demo. Keep examples kid-safe and conservative.
- Add a short FAQ for teachers addressing "how to explain to parents that the assistant may see student text" (legal wants an easy blurb).
- Consider pre-approval flow: teacher can opt-in a class for more permissive assistant behavior (e.g., provide longer worked examples). Store opt-in flag in school mapping.

Random heuristics & ideas to test in pilot:
- Use teacher-injected "nudge phrases" to bias assistant to Socratic questioning rather than direct answers (lower hallucination & supports learning).
- Local micro-cache on device for last 100 student messages to save token spend on repeats and speedup common hints.
- Lightweight on-device reranker (embedding-based) to surface canonical curriculum snippets before hitting the generator.

End of scratchpad — will iterate after follow-ups.
summary: Working notes for Amberwood Academy classroom LLM pilot: constraints (FERPA, intermittent connectivity), proposed edge + hosted fallback architecture, prompt templates, KPIs, and action items.
